Demonstrated experience providing executive administrative support.
1-3 yearsexperience or equivalent training

Under the supervision of the Finance and Human Resources Manager, the Office Manager and Executive Assistant provides administrative and analytical support to manage the business functions and operation of the Office of the University Registrar. Provides support to the University Registrar to ensure timely and accurate flow of information related to official business, projects, and upcoming events. Provides calendar, scheduling, travel, and administrative support to the University Registrar. Interacts professionally and efficiently with all constituencies in person, by telephone, and written communication, including email. Responsible for the University Registrar being on time and fully briefed for meetings. Manages complex system for immediate accessibility of items on request for the University Registrar. Researches and prepares information on highly sensitive issues. Maintains confidentiality at all times.
Solid communication and interpersonal skills to communicate effectively verbally and in writing with the public and members of all levels of the University.
Working knowledge of university structure, organization, policies, and practices, and familiarity with the Family Educational Right to Privacy Act (FERPA).
Solid organizational skills and ability to multi-task with demanding timeframes and rapidly shifting issues-related priorities with long range assignments.
Working knowledge of campus financial (KFS), payroll (UCPath), time recording (TRS), and student information (ARIES) systems.

Working knowledge of common organization-specific and other computer application programs, including Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Teams, Zoom, web browsers, and email. Ability to use both Mac and PC operating systems.
Ability to use discretion and maintain confidentiality.
Ability to comprehend substance of written communications and preserve interrelationships with materials and activities.
Ability to determine, coordinate, and initiate actions on a broad variety of communications and request information.
Ability to analyze administrative problems or issues and recommend appropriate solutions.
Working knowledge of efficient office systems and methods including filing, recording, organizing workflow, and scheduling.
Ability to compose and prepare narratives, graphs, and tables quickly, accurately, and grammatically correctly.
Ability to create and foster professional working relationships with immediate office staff, members of the campus community, and vendors.
Ability to interpret, apply, and enforce policies.
